Rollback returns to the previous registry version, and workers are replaced by draining.

request.title: Live Partials & Finals
request.scope: Replace the request with one long-lived gRPC session per track: partials at p95 ≤ 500 ms and finals at p95 ≤ 1.5 s after end of utterance.
dod: Partials p95 ≤ 500 ms from spoken word to screen, and finals p95 ≤ 1.5 s after end of utterance.
The 500 ms are split by hop: network, chunk wait, queue, compute and delivery.
If a worker dies, the gateway notices within 1 s, reopens the session on another one and replays the current utterance: ≈ 1–2 s without partials and no final lost.
Partials are coalesced to at most 5 per second per stream, and only if the text changed; finals always go out.

caption-bus-por-reunion.title: Per-Meeting Caption Bus
caption-bus-por-reunion.scope: Publish partials and finals from the workers to an in-memory pub/sub (NATS or Redis Pub/Sub), from which the existing WebSocket signaling pushes them to each client.
dod: There is one topic per meeting in an in-memory pub/sub (NATS or Redis Pub/Sub): workers publish and signaling servers consume.
Each message carries `meeting_id`, speaker, `utterance_id`, sequence number, type, and frozen and tentative text; the client replaces by `utterance_id` and drops stale sequences.
The bus keeps each meeting's finals from the last 60 s for clients that reconnect.
`CaptionDeliveryLag` fires when p95 delivery to signaling stays above 250 ms for 10 min.
Only finals from meetings with saving enabled are copied to Kafka; otherwise the text exists only in memory.

monitoreo.title: Per-Hop & Stream Monitoring
monitoreo.scope: Monitor per-hop latency, active streams (also the autoscaling signal), reconnects and voice ratio, with the golden canary measuring WER in production, and retrain on triggers with a quarterly review.
dod: The 8 alerts pass their promtool tests, with a per-hop server budget: `CaptionPartialLatencyHigh` at 200 ms, `CaptionFinalLatencyHigh` at 1.2 s and `GPUStreamSaturation` with the model step above 128 ms.
`SessionReconnectRateHigh` counts only unplanned reconnects (more than 2 % in 15 min), excluding `migrate` and the max duration.
`VADActiveRatioShift` compares the voice ratio with the same hour last week (below 0.7× or above 1.3× for 1 h).
Logs contain no audio or text: only ids, timings and counters.
Retraining is trigger-based (a slice falling behind, a change in input audio, a better model), with a quarterly review.

canary-golden-en-produccion.title: Production Golden Canary
canary-golden-en-produccion.scope: Have a bot join an internal meeting and play golden-set audio to measure end-to-end WER and latency without touching customer audio.
dod: Every few minutes, per region and language, a bot joins an internal meeting and plays golden-set audio as a participant.
It goes through the real path (SFU, gateway, router, worker and bus) and measures end-to-end WER and latency without touching customer audio.
`CanaryWERRegression` fires if the canary version's WER exceeds the stable one's + 1 point, with ≥ 5,000 reference words over 30 min, and the rollout stops.

edge.name: Edge / on-device
edge.summary: The model runs next to the line on a Jetson, because the line cannot wait on the network or stop when the internet drops; the cloud trains and monitors. Nothing in the cloud sits on a part's path: Kubernetes and autoscaling drop out (4 fixed devices on Docker), release becomes OTA to a fleet through the DMZ, and monitoring works without internet.

removed.why: 4 fixed devices do not justify Kubernetes: Docker with a restart policy and a watchdog, and no autoscaling either, since sizing is per device.

kickoff.title: Requirements & Capacity Plan
kickoff.scope: Fix part volume, the 350 ms hard decision deadline, the recall and FP targets and ≥ 72 h offline operation, and size the deadline budget, the per-line device and the FP budget from them.
dod: Production is computed: 2 parts/s × 3,600 s × 16 h = 115,200 parts/day per line (≈ 576 defects at 0.5 %), 460,800/day across the 4 lines.
The 350 ms deadline is split by stage: ≈ 50 ms acquisition, ≈ 20 ms preprocessing, ≤ 120 ms inference, ≈ 10 ms PLC write; ≈ 200 ms expected path with 150 ms of margin.
One Jetson Orin NX 16 GB per line, sized for the deterministic latency of a single inference (≈ 24 % GPU occupancy), not for throughput.
The FP budget comes from inspector capacity: hard cap ≈ 2.8 %, target ≤ 1.5 % (inspector at ≈ 60 %), with recall ≥ 99.5 % per defect type.

datos.title: Line Images & Verdicts
datos.scope: Collect images from the line camera and label them with the inspector's tablet verdict, the cheapest label, starting from ≈ 2,000 good parts and ≈ 300 defects.
dod: Line 1 shadow collects images with the production camera and strobe; at the start there are ≈ 2,000 good parts and ≈ 300 defects.
The inspector labels each diverted part on the tablet with one tap: good, one of the 4 types, or other.
Quality reviews all disagreements and ≈ 5 % of verdicts, and on ≈ 10 % the tablet hides the reason to measure anchoring.
Line images are filtered (high-score ones removed, with an audited sample) before entering the good-parts set.
1 % of passed parts, near-rejects and every escape the OEM reports are also collected.

versionado.title: Snapshots, Golden Sets & Lineage
versionado.scope: Keep immutable snapshots in S3, frozen golden sets per defect type, and part ↔ image ↔ model ↔ decision lineage.
dod: Each label batch produces a snapshot with a manifest (image hash, label, label source and version) and an immutable id in S3.
Per-defect-type golden sets are frozen, never enter training, and are built from defects that did not pass through the model's filter.
Each decision is an immutable record with `decision` and `model_decision`, model version and thresholds, scores, latency and PLC ack.
Labels are events with author and time: never overwritten, corrected with a new one.
commandNotes: List what is under a snapshot prefix (read-only).
If the team already uses DVC: hashes the folder, leaves `{carpeta_datos}.dvc` for git and pushes the data to the S3 remote.
If you use lakeFS: an isolated branch over the bucket, no data copied; then `lakectl commit` and `lakectl merge`.

entrenamiento.title: Cloud Training
entrenamiento.scope: Train in an on-demand cloud GPU job — anomaly detection on good parts and, once there are enough defects, a per-type classifier — monthly or on trigger.
dod: An on-demand cloud GPU job trains the anomaly model on good parts and, once there are hundreds of defects per type, the classifier.
The run is reproducible: data snapshot, commit and container by digest.
It uses the same preprocessing (crop, normalization and tiles) that runs on the Jetson.
The split is by time or by lot, never random.

gate.title: Per-Type Recall & Threshold
gate.scope: Gate on per-defect-type recall at fixed FP on the golden sets, and pick the threshold by expected cost with recall ≥ 99.5 % (`choose_threshold.py`).
dod: Per-defect-type recall is measured at fixed FP on the golden sets, with slices by part variant, line and camera, shift and lot.
`choose_threshold.py` picks the threshold with recall ≥ 99.5 % per type, a 1.5 % FP target and a hard cap of ≈ 2.85 %; if no threshold qualifies, it exits with an error.
With the classifier, each head gets its share of the FP budget (`--target-fp-rate 0.003 --max-fp-rate 0.0057`), and the combination is verified ≤ 1.5 % before writing `config.yaml`.
Recall is reported with its Clopper-Pearson bound: claiming 99.5 % requires ≈ 600 real defects per type with no misses.
If any type does not reach 99.5 %, nothing is built.

export.title: Engine on Identical Jetson
export.scope: Build the engine on a CI Jetson identical to the line devices (same module, JetPack and power mode), with parity against the ONNX and fixed-batch latency.
dod: The TensorRT FP16 engine is built with `build_engine_jetson.sh` on an Orin NX with the same module, JetPack and power mode as the line.
The script checks the mode with `EXPECTED_POWER_MODE` and outputs the `.plan`, the trtexec log and a JSON with the sha256 of the ONNX and of the plan.
The shape is fixed: a batch of 20 tiles of 512 × 512 and a single profile.
Parity against the ONNX passes, and fixed-batch inference fits in ≤ 120 ms measured with trtexec.
Start with FP16; INT8 only if FP16 does not fit, calibrating with defects included.

serving.title: Jetson Inspection Loop
serving.scope: Run a single process on the Jetson Orin NX that acquires the image, builds 20 tiles, runs TensorRT FP16 and writes to the PLC over Modbus TCP, with a deadline guard that writes `DIVERT` when time runs out.
outputs: PASS / REJECT / DIVERT decision written to the PLC
dod: `app.py` measures the deadline from the trigger (trigger + 350 ms) and consumes each trigger's frame even if it arrives late.
`decide()` returns REJECT if any score is ≥ its threshold; a NaN, a score outside [0, 1] or a missing type is DIVERT, never PASS.
If less than ≈ 140 ms remain after the capture, immediate DIVERT; if the 50 ms write does not fit, nothing is written.
A dark image yields `bad_image` (DIVERT), and the watchdog kills the process after 30 s without progress.
The inspector's 62 tests and the threshold tool's 20 pass.

empaquetado.title: arm64 Image with Compose
empaquetado.scope: Build an arm64 image on `l4t-tensorrt` run with `docker compose` (`runtime: nvidia`, host network), with engines mounted separately so the previous one can be restored without network.
dod: The image starts from `nvcr.io/nvidia/l4t-tensorrt:r10.3.0-runtime`, with the same TensorRT as JetPack 6.2.x, and runs as a non-root user.
`docker-compose.yml` uses `runtime: nvidia`, `network_mode: host`, `restart: unless-stopped`, `read_only: true` and `cap_drop: ALL`.
`config.yaml` and `/opt/inspector/models` are mounted read-only: the engine is not inside the image.
The healthcheck reads the heartbeat (reports, does not restart) and logs rotate at 50 MB × 5 files.

cicd.title: Signed Release with Plan
cicd.scope: Register every version signed (ONNX, engine per module and JetPack, thresholds and container) together with its per-line rollout plan.
outputs: signed release with its rollout plan
dod: Each version is registered signed: ONNX, engine per module and JetPack, per-type thresholds, container by digest and gate metrics.
It carries its rollout plan: line 1 in shadow for one shift, line 1 canary, the 4 lines and then the other plants.
`choose_threshold.py` works as a CI gate: without a threshold that meets recall and cap, the pipeline fails.
The inspector and threshold-tool tests pass on Python 3.10, JetPack 6's version.

ota-por-la-dmz.title: OTA via the DMZ
ota-por-la-dmz.scope: Have the DMZ pull signed artifacts over outbound connections, verify the signature and copy them to a local registry on the OT network, so devices never reach the internet.
outputs: artifacts in the local OT registry
dod: The DMZ gateway downloads over outbound connections, verifies the signature and copies the artifacts to the local registry on the OT network.
Devices download only from the local registry and never reach the internet.
Updates go in during the nightly window and, if there is no link, they wait.

rollout.title: Per-Line Shadow & Canary
rollout.scope: Roll out per line: overnight the engine lands in slot B with a smoke test, line 1 runs one shift in shadow, then canary and all 4 lines, with local rollback and no network needed.
dod: Overnight the new engine lands in slot B, next to the current one, and passes a smoke test with golden-part images.
Line 1 runs a full shift in shadow: the challenger only logs, after the champion has written to the PLC.
It advances only if it misses no defect the champion caught, does not raise FPs and has zero deadline misses; quality reviews all disagreements.
Then line 1 decides for several shifts (canary), followed by one wave per line.
Rollback is local and takes minutes: `config.yaml` points back to the previous engine and the container restarts, without network.

request.title: Part Decided in 350 ms
request.scope: Decide each part within a 350 ms deadline from a hardware photocell trigger (2 parts per second per line), with no HTTP in the path.
dod: The photocell triggers the camera in hardware and the PLC assigns the sequence number; within ≈ 50 ms the image is in Jetson memory.
Loop p99.9 stays ≤ 350 ms over full shifts, with the enclosure closed.
The decision goes out as `[part_id, código]` in a single Modbus TCP write, with no retries.
The shape is fixed, there is no dynamic batching, the power mode is fixed and `jetson_clocks` is applied on every boot.
`inspection_latency_seconds` has a bucket at 0.35 s, and `inspection_deadline_miss_total` stays ≈ 0.

plc-con-default-seguro.title: PLC Safe Default
plc-con-default-seguro.scope: Have the PLC pass a part only if a PASS with its number arrived before the deadline, so a dead Jetson, a dead network or a late decision all end the same way: diverted.
dod: The PLC diverts every part without a valid PASS for its `part_id` before the deadline: code 0, no decision, means divert.
The PLC resets the register to 0 after using a decision, because the 16-bit `part_id` repeats every 65,536 parts.
A chute sensor confirms each diverted part; without confirmation, with low air pressure or with the bin full, the PLC stops the line and lights the andon.
Jetson down, network down or a late decision all end the same: the part is diverted.

monitoreo.title: Local Prometheus & Andon
monitoreo.scope: Run Prometheus and the andon in the plant because there may be no internet, shipping heartbeats and aggregates to the cloud; a reject rate above 2× its baseline for 30 min most likely means light, lens or focus, not defects.
dod: `app.py` exports its 7 metrics with series at 0 from startup, and DIVERTs are counted by their 10 reasons.
Paging alerts are evaluated in the plant's Prometheus and Alertmanager, and reach the andon and the maintenance tablet.
`RejectRateSpike` fires with REJECTs above 2× their 7-day baseline for 30 min, without mixing in DIVERTs.
`AnomalyScoreDrift` compares the last hour's median against the 7-day one + 0.1, for 2 h.
Cloud `DeviceOffline` alerts only during shift hours and if the plant gateway is reporting; if the gateway is missing, it is a single link ticket.

store-and-forward-a-la-nube.title: Store-and-Forward to Cloud
store-and-forward-a-la-nube.scope: Hold decisions, reject images and verdicts in the plant store and upload them when the link is up, so the line runs ≥ 72 h without internet.
inputs: decision records, reject images and verdicts
dod: The plant store keeps decision records, reject images, the passed-part sample and verdicts, and the line runs ≥ 72 h without internet.
Upload is idempotent (each record with an id, each image named by its hash) and resumes where it left off.
Records and verdicts upload first, then rejects and finally the sample, with a bandwidth cap during shifts.
The store holds weeks (≈ 69 GB/day) and sync lag is measured.
With the disk full, what is already synced is dropped first; decision records never.

piezas-patron-en-cada-turno.title: Golden Parts Every Shift
piezas-patron-en-cada-turno.scope: Start every shift with known good and defective parts and give no part a PASS until that check passes, catching a dirty lens, a shifted focus or degraded light before production.
dod: Each shift starts with the station's golden parts (2 good and 1 of each defect type), with the line in golden mode.
Defective parts are rejected and good ones pass at least 0.15 below the anomaly threshold.
Until the check passes in that process, no part gets PASS, and the approval expires at the start of the next shift.
`GoldenPartCheckFailed` fires with `golden_part_check_ok == 0` for 10 min during shift hours.
Each bad golden part must be confirmed in the bin: this also tests the chute sensor.
